desc:
A directed graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1; each edges[i] = [from, to, w] is a one-way edge with weight w, possibly negative. A walk may repeat nodes and edges.

Walk costs are summed edge weights. Starting from src, a node v is called unbounded if walks from src to v can be made as cheap as you like, which happens exactly when some walk from src to v passes through a cycle of negative total weight. Return the labels of all unbounded nodes in increasing order (an empty array if there are none). Nodes that cannot be reached from src are not unbounded, and src itself counts as unbounded if some walk from src back to src passes through a negative cycle.

Example: n = 5, edges = [[0,1,2],[1,2,-3],[2,1,1],[2,3,4],[4,0,1]], src = 0. The cycle 1 → 2 → 1 has weight -2, so nodes 1 and 2 get cheaper with every lap, and node 3 hangs off node 2. Node 0 is fine (cost 0) and node 4 is unreachable. The answer is [1, 2, 3].
constraints: edges[i] = [from, to, w] with 0 ≤ from, to < n and -1,000 ≤ w ≤ 1,000
Each ordered pair (from, to) appears at most once; from may equal to
hints: Plain Bellman-Ford only tells you whether some negative cycle is reachable. You need to know which nodes are affected by it.
After n - 1 rounds of relaxation from src, every node whose distance is still final is correct. If an edge (u, v, w) can still be relaxed, then v can be reached through a negative cycle.

Collect every node v that can still be relaxed after n - 1 rounds (with u reachable), then run a BFS/DFS from all of them along the edges. Every node reached is unbounded, because after reaching the cycle you can loop forever and then continue to it. Sort the result.
editorial: Run n - 1 rounds of Bellman-Ford from src, ignoring edges that start at nodes not yet reached. Nodes that are not influenced by any reachable negative cycle have their true distance by now. Do one more pass and mark each node v for which some edge (u, v, w) with reached u still improves dist[v]. Every such v is unbounded, since a simple route would already be final, so the improvement must come from a walk that uses a negative cycle. Moreover each reachable negative cycle contains at least one such node: if all edges of the cycle satisfied dist[u] + w ≥ dist[v], adding these inequalities around the cycle would force its weight to be non-negative.

Unboundedness then spreads along edges: if v is unbounded and v → x is an edge, x is unbounded as well. A single multi-source BFS from the marked nodes reaches exactly the unbounded nodes (every node of a negative cycle is reached from the marked one on it). The algorithm costs O(n · E) for Bellman-Ford plus O(n + E) for the search. A common mistake is marking only the nodes relaxed in the extra pass, which misses downstream nodes such as node 3 in the example.
